**Checked by:** audit cycle 25 (CE2) — DRIVEN in a real browser

**Code evidence:**

- 386 tests pass across the projection / compression / codegraph / tool-group modules (1 unrelated skip)

**Driven in the UI:** Drove #/tools. The header reads 'Tool groups · 11 groups, 110 tools' with a switch, and the explanation states the economics exactly: 'Every tool schema an agent carries costs context on every turn. Groups let a session load only the groups it needs and pick up the rest on demand — the agent activates them itself mid-task.' Beneath it, the atom's SC#8 guarantee is surfaced to the user verbatim: 'Nothing is ever unavailable — a tool stays callable by name even when its group is not loaded, and the agent can search across all of them.'

**Notes:** That second sentence is the load-bearing one. A grouping mechanism that could make a tool UNREACHABLE would be a capability regression dressed as an optimisation; saying plainly that a tool stays callable by name is what makes the whole feature safe to turn on. It is also the claim most likely to rot, and it is stated where a user can hold the product to it.
